answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers (RLN) cap how many times one staked agent may act each epoch. Registration locks a bond and mints a zero-knowledge credential; every action embeds a Shamir share of the agent secret keyed to a per-epoch counter. Exceed the limit and two shares collide, reconstructing the key so anyone can slash the bond. One thread of over-posting unravels the identity that sent it, and a whole lagoon of cloned agents each needs its own forfeitable stake, so the credential is a self-burning fuse, not a reusable relic to copy across fakes.
